source: Your spellbook gains a mind and becomes your spellcasting focus. When you cast a wizard spell with a slot you can change its damage type to one found in another spell in your book of the slot's level; once per long rest you can cast a ritual spell from the book at its normal casting time rather than adding 10 minutes; and over a short rest your quill can turn a blank book into a new home for its mind.

As a bonus action, manifest your spellbook's mind as a Tiny spectral object within 60 feet that sheds dim light in 10 feet, sees in darkness to 60 feet and moves up to 30 feet when you use a bonus action; it ends if it is ever more than 300 feet from you. While it is manifested you can cast a wizard spell from its space a number of times per long rest equal to your proficiency bonus. Manifesting it is free once per long rest, or costs a spell slot of any level.

After a long rest you can create a magic scroll of a 1st- or 2nd-level wizard spell from your book with a casting time of an action; it is cast as if one level higher, and it vanishes once cast or when you finish a long rest.

While your spellbook is on your person you have advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks. If you take damage while the book's mind is manifested, a reaction dismisses it to prevent all of that damage; then roll 3d6, and spells in your book with a combined level at least that total vanish from it until you finish 1d6 long rests (if there aren't enough, you drop to 0 hit points). Once per long rest.
An artificer who works in tinctures and reagents, healing allies and corroding enemies with thrown concoctions.

After a long rest you brew one elixir in an empty flask (two from 6th level, three from 15th), its effect rolled on a d6: healing (2d4 + your Intelligence modifier hit points), swiftness (walking speed 10 feet higher for an hour), resilience (+1 AC for 10 minutes), boldness (a d4 added to attack rolls and saving throws for a minute), flight (a 10-foot flying speed for 10 minutes) or transformation (alter self for 10 minutes). As an action you can expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to brew one more, choosing its effect. An elixir lasts until it is drunk or you finish a long rest.

When you cast a spell with alchemist's supplies as your spellcasting focus, add your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to one roll of the spell that restores hit points or deals acid, fire, necrotic or poison damage.

A creature that drinks one of your experimental elixirs also gains 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier temporary hit points (minimum 1). With alchemist's supplies as your focus you can cast lesser restoration without a spell slot or preparing it, a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.
You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, immunity to the poisoned condition, and can cast greater restoration and heal once per long rest each without a slot.
An artificer who lives inside their own powered armor, built either to guard the line or to strike from the dark.
Proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
Your armor becomes a magical suit that needs no Strength, cannot be removed against your will, and replaces missing limbs.

Choose Guardian or Infiltrator, and change it on a short or long rest; you use Intelligence for the attack and damage rolls of the armor's weapon. Guardian: thunder gauntlets (a 1d8 thunder melee weapon; a creature hit has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you until the start of your next turn) and Defensive Field (a bonus action gives you temporary hit points equal to your artificer level, a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest). Infiltrator: a lightning launcher (a 1d6 lightning ranged weapon, 90/300 feet, that once on each of your turns deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage to a creature it strikes), Powered Steps (walking speed 5 feet higher) and Dampening Field (advantage on Stealth checks).
Attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.

Your Arcane Armor counts as separate items for your infusions (the armor, the boots, the helmet and the special weapon), and you can infuse two more items at once, provided both are parts of the armor.

Guardian: when a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, a reaction makes it save on Strength against your spell save DC or be pulled up to 25 feet toward you into an unoccupied space, and if it ends within 5 feet of you, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of the reaction; a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest. Infiltrator: a creature your lightning launcher damages glows until the start of your next turn, has disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and the next attack roll against it has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage if it hits.
An artificer who builds a small arcane cannon and turns a fight into a siege.
